item.text:
The target OM-classifier obligation is not proved. The semantic-classifier argument is largely sound, including at wild primes, but the attempted reduction to the actual classifier contains a false equivalence and leaves the decisive certification lemma open.

1. **CRITICAL ERROR — pointwise certification is not equivalent to Haar-a.e. certification.**

> “By Lemma A, for `c^OM` the row is EQUIVALENT to:  
> **OPEN LEMMA OL1 …** For … every monic separable `f` … there is `N(f)`…”

Lemma A gives
\[
\mu\{a:\text{no level decides }a\}=0,
\]
which means certification for almost every coefficient vector. OL1 demands certification at every separable vector. A classifier may fail forever on a nonempty Haar-null subset of the separable locus while still satisfying `env(N) → 0`. Thus OL1 is sufficient, not equivalent. Proposition 5.1 later states only `OL1 ⇒ env → 0`, contradicting the earlier equivalence claim.

2. **CRITICAL ERROR — the actual OM obligation is explicitly left open.**

> “What remains corpus-specific: that the project's certification predicate … *accepts* at this `N(f)` … it is NOT discharged here.”

This is precisely the bridge required by the problem: termination of an idealized OM algorithm does not show that the constructed level-\(N\) classifier emits a verdict. Since OL1-ii is open, neither pointwise nor almost-everywhere certification of the intended classifier has been established.

The final admission is therefore accurate:

> “Nothing here is a complete proof of the Lean row at the constructed instance…”

Consequently this cannot verify M05-exhaust.

3. **JUSTIFICATION GAP — “finite run” does not automatically imply a finite stable certificate.**

> “A terminated run makes finitely many inspections, so all its witnesses fit below some finite `N(f)`, and the run — hence the verdict — is constant on the level-`N(f)` class.”

This needs substantially more than finiteness. Newton-polygon construction can involve zero coefficients, infinite valuations, cancellations, equality cases, representative changes, and policy-dependent refinements. One must show that each successful branch has a finite, perturbation-stable certificate and that the concrete classifier recognizes it. The assertion that all inspected quantities are suitable “`Z`-polynomials” in the original coefficients is also not established for recursively chosen key polynomials and residue-tower representatives.

4. **JUSTIFICATION GAP — the cited GMN result does not justify the stated step bound as written.**

> “Corollary 4.19: … the OM descent terminates at finite order — at most `ind(f) ≤ v_p(disc f)/2` nontrivial steps.”

The index theorem and Corollary 4.19 support eventual completeness of higher-order types for separable polynomials. The stronger operational claim that the canonical algorithm performs at most `ind(f)` “nontrivial steps” requires a definition of steps and an argument charging every refinement/iteration to positive index growth. Finite order is not automatically a bound on all representative/recentering iterations.

5. **Lemma A itself is sound.**

> “`env(N) → 0 ⇔ μ(⋂_N U_N)=0 ⇔` for `μ`-a.e. `a`, some level decides `a`.”

The cylinder-mass identity, antitonicity from stability, and continuity from above are correct. The error occurs only when this almost-everywhere statement is replaced by OL1’s pointwise statement.

6. **Lemma B is sound.**

> “the discriminant … has degree exactly `n−1` as a polynomial in `a_0`, with `a_0`-leading coefficient `±n^n`.”

Using
\[
\operatorname{Res}(f',f)=n^n\prod_{f'(\theta)=0}f(\theta)
\]
gives exactly \(n-1\) factors affine and monic in \(a_0\). Hence the \(a_0\)-leading coefficient is \(n^n\), up to the discriminant sign. No cancellation is possible.

7. **Lemma C’s exponent arithmetic is sound.**

> “\((n−1)\,p^{-\max(0,\lceil(m-w)/(n−1)\rceil)}\), with \(w=n\,v_p(n)\).”

The one-variable root-cover argument yields the stated exponent after taking \(d=n-1\) and \(v(\operatorname{lc})=v(n^n)=n\,v_p(n)\). Slicing in \(a_0\) is legitimate because Lemma B makes the degree and leading coefficient independent of the other coefficients. The conclusion that the discriminant-zero locus is Haar-null follows by intersecting the valuation tails.

8. **The semantic-classifier rate does hold at wild primes, but it says nothing quantitative about the intended classifier.**

For fixed \(n\) and any prime \(p\mid n\), the wild term
\[
w=n\,v_p(n)
\]
is a finite additive shift. Therefore the displayed semantic bound still tends to zero like \(p^{-N/(2(n-1))}\), up to a fixed multiplicative constant. No tame assumption is used in Lemmas B–D.

But:

> “OL2 (rates for `c^OM`) stated, literature candidate … UNVERIFIED.”

Therefore no rate—indeed no qualitative drainage—is proved here for the constructed OM classifier at wild primes. The cited complexity paper does contain a finite-precision result: its Theorem 3.13 states that precision \(\delta+1\) preserves OM factorizations for congruent separable polynomials. That still requires a faithfulness proof connecting its algorithm and certificates to this project’s canonical classifier. [Bauch–Nart–Stainsby, Theorem 3.13](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/79A4A904C75E875A78F0671E0AF92D9A/S1461157013000089a.pdf/complexity_of_om_factorizations_of_polynomials_over_local_fields.pdf)

9. **CRITICAL ERROR — T5 draws a lower bound for the semantic classifier from an upper-bound superset.**

> “documents that no better-than-`p^{-N/2}` envelope for the SEMANTIC classifier is possible at `n=2` … the gap is real”

The proof only establishes
\[
U_N^{\rm sem}\subseteq\{v(\operatorname{disc})\ge\lceil N/2\rceil\}.
\]
Showing that the set on the right has measure of order \(p^{-N/2}\) supplies no lower bound on \(U_N^{\rm sem}\). The inclusion may be very loose. Thus the claimed optimality and “real gap” do not follow from T5.

The numeric tests cannot repair any of these logical defects; they test discriminant-tail supersets, not the actual general-\(n\) OM certification predicate.

VERDICT: UNSOUND
